proposals.before: The vice censor-in-chief said, "Among lower officials during the puppet Chu regime, men such as Yu Mo and Wang Tingxiu were not ill but resolutely resigned their posts and returned to the Song. I ask that they be rewarded and promoted."
proposals.after: The vice censor-in-chief said, "Among lower officials during the puppet Chu regime, men such as Yu Mo and Wang Tingxiu were not ill but resolutely resigned their posts and went home. I ask that they be rewarded and promoted."
proposals.reason: Chinese 致為臣而歸 means they resigned and returned home; the idiomatic English invents 'to the Song', which is not in the source.

proposals.before: After he and Zheng Jue had forcefully opposed demoting and enfeoffing Gaozong, before long he was sent out to govern Ruizhou. proposals.after: After he and Zheng Jue had forcefully opposed reducing Gaozong's titles, before long he was sent out to govern Ruizhou. Right Remonstrance Officer Lü Zhi memorialized: "If today the court transfers a remonstrance officer because of a dispute with a chief minister, and tomorrow dismisses a remonstrance officer, then when chief ministers err hereafter, who will dare speak?"
proposals.reason: 降封高宗事 is a dispute over reducing Gaozong's titles, not jointly 'demoting and enfeoffing' him.

Send twenty thousand elite troops—one column from Shouyang, one from the Han River—straight for the old capital, and the enemy should withdraw without a fight. proposals.reason: 樞密使 is Military Affairs Commissioner (shumishi), not 'Bureau director'.

proposals.before: At that time the cave tribes and Liao were not yet pacified; he was advanced to Direct Academician and made Hunan Pacification Commissioner, forbade illicit coiners, urged people to farm, prices were stabilized, and merchants then traveled freely.
proposals.after: At that time the cave tribes were not yet pacified; he was advanced to Direct Academician and made Hunan Pacification Commissioner, forbade illicit coiners, urged people to farm, prices were stabilized, and merchants then traveled freely.
proposals.reason: 峒獠 names southwestern hill peoples; 獠 is not the Khitan Liao dynasty. The literal rendering invents a second group “Liao.”

proposals.before: He planned to return south. Suddenly he heard that Bangchang had been sent to distant prefectures and that petty men were being dismissed one after another—seventeen or eighteen matching what he had urged—and Deng rejoiced, "Now I may speak fully."
proposals.after: He planned to return south. Suddenly he heard that Bangchang had been sent to distant prefectures and that petty men were being dismissed one after another—seven or eight in ten matching what he had urged—and Deng rejoiced, "Now I may speak fully."
proposals.reason: 十七八 means roughly seventy to eighty percent, not the cardinal numbers seventeen or eighteen.

proposals.before: He therefore planned to return south; suddenly he heard that Bangchang had each been given distant prefectures and that petty men of the moment were dismissed one after another—seventeen or eight out of ten matching what he had said—and Deng rejoiced: "Now one may speak fully."
proposals.after: He therefore planned to return south; suddenly he heard that Bangchang had been given a distant prefecture and that petty men of the moment were dismissed one after another—seven or eight out of ten matching what he had said—and Deng rejoiced: "Now one may speak fully."
proposals.reason: 十七八 is an approximate fraction (seven or eight tenths). “Seventeen or eight out of ten” is a fused mistranslation; 各與遠郡 refers to assigning distant prefectures, not a literal “each” attached only to Bangchang as “had each.”

proposals.before: Deng declined but could not refuse. With nowhere else to put the money, he placed it with the school and bought books to thank the people.
proposals.after: Deng declined but could not refuse. With nowhere else to put the money, he asked that it be placed with the school and used to buy books to thank the scholars and people.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 請 ('asked that it be placed') and 士民 ('scholars and people'); the Chinese is a request to lodge the gift with the school, not a completed placement by Deng alone.

proposals.before: Cultured sons and cultured grandsons, fit to be rulers and kings, suffered calamities, cut off like a belt's end.
proposals.after: Cultured sons and cultured grandsons, fit to be rulers and kings, met with calamities, yet were not cut off, continuing like a sash.
proposals.reason: Literal reverses 不斷如帶: the line is unbroken like a belt/sash, not 'cut off like a belt's end'.

proposals.before: Your servant is truly reckless; last year he submitted a memorial requesting Your Majesty to take a worthy Taizu grandson, treat his rank as imperial prince, and let him govern the nine provinces; he mistakenly received adoption and hearing and was pardoned rather than executed.
proposals.after: Your servant is truly reckless; last year he submitted a memorial requesting Your Majesty to take a worthy Taizu grandson, treat his rank as imperial prince, and let him govern the nine provinces; he mistakenly received a hearing of his proposal and was pardoned rather than executed.
proposals.reason: 采聽 means the throne adopted/heeded the memorial, not legal or familial ‘adoption’.

proposals.before: Chief councilor Qin Hui, whom Fu Zhirou had recommended, hated him and prompted critics to charge Yinliang with concealing his father's death. The Court of Judicial Review found no truth in it, yet he was still dismissed for a clansman's falsely occupying an official household register and sent to the Ministry of Personnel—thereby ruined.
proposals.after: Chief councilor Qin Hui, because Fu Zhirou had recommended him, hated him and prompted critics to charge Yinliang with concealing his father's death. The Court of Judicial Review found no truth in it, yet he was still dismissed for a clansman's falsely occupying an official household register and sent to the Ministry of Personnel—thereby ruined.
proposals.reason: 以其直柔所薦 marks Yinliang as Fu Zhirou’s recommendee, the reason Qin Hui hated him; neighboring narrative has Fu Zhirou recommending Yinliang, not Qin Hui.

proposals.before: Chief Councilor Qin Hui, whom Zhirou had recommended for his bluntness, hated him; he prompted critics to impeach Yinliang for concealing his father's death without reporting mourning; the case went to the Court of Judicial Review for interrogation and was unfounded, yet he was still punished for a clansman's falsely occupying an official household register, dismissed, and sent to the Ministry of Personnel—thereby ruined.
proposals.after: Chief Councilor Qin Hui, because Zhirou had recommended him, hated him; he prompted critics to impeach Yinliang for concealing his father's death without reporting mourning; the case went to the Court of Judicial Review for interrogation and was unfounded, yet he was still punished for a clansman's falsely occupying an official household register, dismissed, and sent to the Ministry of Personnel—thereby ruined.
proposals.reason: 直柔 is the personal name Zhirou, not ‘bluntness’; 以…所薦 is the causal ‘because he was the man Zhirou recommended’.
